title: Facile thermal desolvation of Ce2(OPri)8(PriOH)2: Characterization and molecular structure of Ce4(μ4-O)(μ3-OPri)2(μ-OPri)4(OPri)8

synthesis.procedure: All manipulations were carried out under argon using Schlenk tubes and vacuum-line techniques. Ce2(OPri)8(PriOH)2 (2 g, 2.3 mmol), prepared as reported in the literature, was heated in the solid state for about 15 min at 70 °C / 10^-3 mm Hg. The yellow solid became pasty and was dissolved in DME–PriOH (2/3 by volume). Orange crystals of Ce4O(OPri)14 (0.7 g, 43%) and Ce2(OPri)8(PriOH)2 were separated by crystallization at −10 °C. The same oxo compound was also obtained by refluxing Ce2(OPri)8(PriOH)2 in toluene for ca 1.5 h (yellow solution turns orange immediately; yield ~25%). The oxo species is soluble in common solvents including isopropanol and hexane; m.p. 145 °C, decomposition at 170 °C.
synthesis.temperature: 70 °C (solid-state heating); crystallization at −10 °C; alternative reflux in toluene
synthesis.vessel_or_method: Schlenk tubes and vacuum-line techniques under argon; thermal desolvation of the solid at 70 °C / 10^-3 mm Hg, or reflux in toluene
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Pasty yellow residue dissolved in DME–PriOH (2/3 v/v); orange crystals of the oxo cluster separated from remaining Ce2(OPri)8(PriOH)2 by crystallization at −10 °C.
